predecessors.name: Kushan Empire
predecessors.text: Haryana, eastern Punjab and northern Rajasthan, Kushan land until the Yaudheya blow

successors.name: Gupta Empire
successors.text: the whole Yaudheya shape: Cliopatria's Gupta shape of 378 is the 358 shape plus these 840 cells

ledger.x: c. 200: the Yaudheyas rule themselves between the Sutlej and the Jumna after the Kushan blow. Yaudheya page: 'in approximately 180 CE' (Majumdar) the Yaudheyas and allied janapadas dealt a blow to the Kushans, after which the Kushans ceased to be present in Eastern Punjab; post-Kushan coins with 3rd- or 4th-century…

c. 270: the Kushan land of the upper Ganges and Jumna country becomes Yaudheya. Kushan Empire page (opened 2026-10-19): 'Around 270 their territories on the Gangetic plain became independent under local dynasties such as the Yaudheyas.' Cliopatria's Eastern Kushans drop 818 Yaudheya cells in 270 (eastern-kushans…

c. 306: the Yaudheyas take 230 cells from the Western Satraps' shape. Cliopatria's Yaudheya row begins in 306 and the Western Satraps shape drops those cells in the same year (western-satraps /ledger/11). Yaudheya page: Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription (c. 150) says he 'by force destroyed the Yaudheyas who were loath…

c. 347: the Yaudheyas become Samudragupta's tributaries. Samudragupta page: the Yaudheyas 'seem to have become Samudragupta's tributaries'; the Yaudheya page, on the Allahabad Pillar: their rule was 'propitiated with the payment of all tributes', without armed resistance (Upinder Singh: no troops supplied). The year…

c. 377: the tribute ends with the state: the Gupta shape absorbs the republic (gupta-empire /ledger gain and vassal_end, 378). The Chandragupta II page (opened 2026-10-19) does not mention the Yaudheyas, and no page dates the end. Added 2026-10-19.

c. 377: the Yaudheya republic ends in the Gupta Empire. The Gupta Empire page lists 'Yaudheya' among the empire's predecessors; the Yaudheya page gives 'Disestablished: 4th century CE' and the Gupta Empire as successor in its infobox. wars.outcome: The Yaudheyas and allied janapadas dealt a blow to the Kushans c.

wars.name: Samudragupta's subjugation of the Yaudheyas
wars.outcome: The Allahabad Pillar lists the Yaudheyas among the tributaries; they paid tribute without armed resistance, and Upinder Singh notes no troops were supplied.

certainty.note: The pages give coin-hoard areas (Saharanpur to Bahawalpur, Sutlej to Jumna), no frontier line; the whole life is soft.
